newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IMF to send "technical" mission to Romania this wk.
newsitem.headline: IMF to send "technical" mission to Romania this wk.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund will send a technical mission to Romania this week but will not conduct negotiations on releasing blocked loan funds, an IMF official said on Monday.
"This is a technical, fact-finding mission to assess developments," the official told Reuters from IMF headquarters in Washington.
"But there will be no negotiations, we will not discuss issues for review of the loan programme," he added.

The IMF blocked the release of hefty loan tranches in February after the Romanian government failed to liberalise the foreign exchange market. The government has since placed even tougher restrictions on the market's functions.
Under a standby agreement due to expire in April 1997, the IMF had offered Romania some $280 million in loans.
The IMF said it will not make a formal visit to Romania until the foreign exchange restrictions are eased.

"This visit has nothing to do with the review. There has been no change to our policy of what's needed to unlock the review. Don't see this as a sign of things changing," said the official, who asked not to be named.
The mission, expected to last less than a week, will be headed by Paul Thomsen, IMF chief negotiator for Romania. The last such visit was in June. -- Bucharest newsroom - 40-1 3120264
